biological.citation: Astrocytic LRP1 enables mitochondria transfer to neurons and mitigates brain ischemic stroke by suppressing ARF1 lactylation (PMID: 38906140)
biological.summary: LRP1 in astrocytes suppresses glucose uptake, glycolysis, and lactate production, leading to reduced ARF1 lactylation and promotion of astrocyte-to-neuron mitochondria transfer. LRP1 knockdown reduced mitochondria transfer and worsened ischemia-reperfusion injury in mouse stroke models. Elevated CSF lactate in stroke patients inversely correlated with astrocytic mitochondria.
biological.sample_size: Mouse ischemic stroke model; human stroke patients

biological.citation: Rapid amyloid-β clearance and cognitive recovery through multivalent modulation of blood-brain barrier transport (PMID: 41052971)
biological.summary: LRP1 on the blood-brain barrier mediates transcytosis and clearance of amyloid-β. LRP1-targeted polymersomes upregulated LRP1 expression and promoted efficient Aβ removal, reducing brain Aβ levels by 45% and increasing plasma Aβ 8-fold within 2 hours in AD model mice. Cognitive improvements persisted for 6 months post-treatment.
biological.significance: 45% reduction in brain Aβ; 8-fold increase in plasma Aβ; cognitive performance comparable to wild-type

biological.citation: LRP1 is a neuronal receptor for α-synuclein uptake and spread (PMID: 36056345)
biological.summary: LRP1 mediates neuronal uptake of α-synuclein monomers, oligomers, and pre-formed fibrils through lysine residues and N-terminus interactions. LRP1-knockout iPSC-derived neurons showed significantly reduced α-Syn uptake. In Lrp1-nKO mice, α-Syn spread was significantly reduced compared to wild-type littermates.
biological.sample_size: iPSC-derived neurons; Lrp1-nKO mice at 6 months of age
biological.significance: Significantly reduced uptake in LRP1-KO iPSNs; significantly reduced spread in Lrp1-nKO mice

biological.citation: Inhibiting DNA methylation alleviates cisplatin-induced hearing loss by decreasing oxidative stress-induced mitochondria-dependent apoptosis via the LRP1-PI3K/AKT pathway (PMID: 35530135)
biological.summary: LRP1 is a key component of the LRP1-PI3K/AKT signaling pathway that protects against cisplatin-induced ototoxicity. DNMT inhibitor RG108 increased LRP1 expression and decreased LRP1 promoter methylation, triggering PI3K/AKT pathway activation and reducing apoptosis in hair cells and spiral ganglion neurons.
biological.significance: RG108 markedly reduced cisplatin-induced damage; upregulated BCL-2 and downregulated pro-apoptotic genes

biological.citation: Genome-wide CRISPR screening identifies LRP1 as an entry factor for SFTSV (PMID: 40301361)
biological.summary: LRP1 functions as a host entry receptor for Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome Virus (SFTSV). SFTSV glycoprotein Gn interacts with LRP1 via CLI and CLII domains. LRP1 knockdown/knockout significantly attenuated SFTSV infection in MEFs; LRP1-neutralizing antibody reduced viral load and improved survival in lethal mouse model.
biological.sample_size: Mouse embryonic fibroblasts; lethal male mouse model
biological.significance: Significantly attenuated SFTSV infection with LRP1 inhibition; improved survival in vivo

biological.citation: Role of LRP1 in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease: evidence from clinical and preclinical studies (PMID: 28381441)
biological.summary: LRP1 regulates amyloid-β metabolism in brain and periphery and maintains brain homeostasis through both Aβ-dependent and -independent pathways. LRP1 also regulates pathogenic roles of apoE, the strongest genetic risk factor for AD. Preclinical studies demonstrate LRP1's involvement in AD pathogenesis, though clinical evidence remains insufficient.
biological.sample_size: Review of clinical and preclinical studies over 25 years
biological.significance: Accumulating evidence from preclinical studies; clinical evidence not yet conclusive

biological.citation: LRP1 in GABAergic neurons is a key link between obesity and memory function (PMID: 38636794)
biological.summary: LRP1 in GABAergic neurons regulates energy homeostasis and memory function. Vgat-Cre; LRP1loxP/loxP mice lacking LRP1 in GABAergic neurons developed severe obesity and showed age-dependent impairment in spatial memory, learning, and fear conditioning at 32 weeks. Memory deficits negatively correlated with metabolic risk parameters including body weight, leptin, and insulin.
biological.sample_size: Vgat-Cre; LRP1loxP/loxP mice at 16 and 32 weeks of age
biological.significance: Significant impairment in memory function at 32 weeks; negative correlations with metabolic parameters

biological.citation: Loss of LRP1 Promotes Hepatocellular Carcinoma Progression via UFL1-Mediated Activation of NF-κB Signaling (PMID: 39405202)
biological.summary: LRP1 suppresses hepatocellular carcinoma progression by stabilizing OGA protein and suppressing NF-κB signaling. LRP1 knockdown promotes UFL1-mediated OGA degradation, increasing O-GlcNAcylation of NF-κB and inhibiting pro-apoptotic gene expression. Lower LRP1 levels associate with malignant progression and poor prognosis in HCC patients.
biological.sample_size: HCC patient samples; HCC cell lines; in vivo mouse models
biological.significance: LRP1 knockdown enhanced tumorigenicity; overexpression had opposite effect

biological.citation: Oropouche orthobunyavirus infection is mediated by the cellular host factor Lrp1 (PMID: 35939689)
biological.summary: LRP1 serves as a host entry receptor for Oropouche orthobunyavirus (OROV). OROV glycoproteins bind to LRP1 ectodomain in vitro. LRP1 antagonists and neutralizing antibodies effectively attenuate OROV infection in cells. RAP treatment in lethal mouse model reduced viral load and improved survival.
biological.sample_size: Cell culture; lethal male mouse model
biological.significance: Significantly reduced OROV infection with LRP1 inhibition; improved survival in vivo

biological.citation: Heterozygous LRP1 deficiency causes developmental dysplasia of the hip by impairing triradiate chondrocytes differentiation due to inhibition of autophagy (PMID: 36067312)
biological.summary: LRP1 is essential for normal chondrocyte differentiation and hip development. Heterozygous Lrp1 knockout mice and Lrp1R1783W knockin mice recapitulated human developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) phenotypes. LRP1 deficiency decreased autophagy and increased β-catenin, suppressing chondrocyte marker genes. Pathogenic LRP1 variants identified in DDH families and sporadic patients.
biological.sample_size: 8 DDH families; 68 sporadic DDH patients; Lrp1+/- and Lrp1R1783W mice
biological.significance: Likely pathogenic variants in LRP1 identified in 2 families and 7 unrelated patients; phenotypes recapitulated in mouse models

biological.citation: ASHG 2022 - Genome-wide association meta-analysis reveals 99 risk loci for pain susceptibility and pleiotropic relationships with psychiatric, metabolic, and immunological traits (E. Mocci et al.)
biological.summary: LRP1 locus at 12q13.3 identified as a genome-wide significant risk locus for pain susceptibility in meta-analysis of 17 pain-related traits. The locus showed the strongest joint p-value (6.8e-72) and reached genome-wide significance in all leave-one-trait-out analyses, indicating robust association across multiple pain phenotypes.
biological.sample_size: UK Biobank; meta-analysis of 17 pain susceptibility traits
biological.significance: P-value 6.8e-72; reached genome-wide significance in all leave-one-trait-out analyses
